entries.clue: Fish-eater's oversize – kill! (6)

blocks.note: OS is the clothing-label abbreviation for outsize
a kill is the prey an animal has caught

annotation.surface: A cry from someone watching an oversized fish-eater pounce on its catch.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but is really 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'kill' is a noun here, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: The osprey is a bird of prey that lives almost entirely on fish.

entries.clue: Plastic pipes: too contrary (8)

indicatorNotes.Plastic: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A plumber grumbling that plastic pipes are too awkward to work with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like the material the pipes are made of, but it is the instruction to remould the next letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Contrary and opposite both mean facing the other way.

entries.clue: OAP in trouble – but upright? (5)

indicatorNotes.trouble: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: OAP (old-age pensioner) plus IN, the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A pensioner has had a fall, yet somehow is still standing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of 'in trouble' but is fodder. An upright is a piano whose strings run vertically, as opposed to a grand.
annotation.definitionFit: An upright is the everyday name for a vertical piano.

entries.clue: Organ on creepy type that sticks in your head (7)

annotation.definition: Organ on creepy type that sticks in your head

blocks.note: the ear is an organ
a worm is a creepy-crawly and a creep

annotation.surface: A horror-film image of something crawling into a body part and lodging in the brain.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts EAR above WORM. The whole clue also describes the answer: a tune that gets into your ear and won't leave.
annotation.definitionFit: An earworm is a catchy tune that keeps replaying in your head.

entries.clue: Extensive cock up with Oasis concert initially (8)

indicatorNotes.cock: to cock something up is to mess it up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: used as it stands
used as it stands
first letter of concert

annotation.surface: A review complaining that an Oasis gig was a huge mess.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cock up' reads as one phrase, but 'cock' is the jumbling instruction and 'up' is among the letters jumbled. Oasis are a British rock band.
annotation.definitionFit: Something spacious is extensive, with plenty of room.

entries.clue: God welcomes a good heathen! (5)

indicatorNotes.welcomes: to welcome is to take in, so the god holds the other letters

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
used as it stands
G is the standard abbreviation for good

annotation.surface: A charitable deity opening his arms to an unbeliever.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that a god should welcome a heathen at all.
annotation.definitionFit: A pagan is a heathen, someone outside the main religions.

entries.clue: Body calling for new cash point on island (7)

indicatorNotes.new: a new version of the word is a remade one, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.on: placed next to, so the point is followed by the island

blocks.note: CASH rearranged
S (south) is a compass point
IS is the standard abbreviation for island

annotation.surface: A person demanding fresh money from a cash machine on holiday somewhere remote.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cash point' reads as a cash machine, but splits into 'cash' to rearrange and 'point', a compass direction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the chassis is a car's body frame, the part everything else is bolted to.

entries.clue: Topless at the Commons, everybody welcome? (4,5)

blocks.note: without a top, like an open-topped car
the Commons is the lower House of the UK Parliament

annotation.surface: A scandal: someone baring all in the House of Commons, and nobody objects.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topless' suggests nudity but means only uncovered. The House of Commons is the elected chamber of the UK Parliament.
annotation.definitionFit: An open house is an event where everybody is welcome to drop in.

entries.clue: Just a couple of drops of semen and boyfriend gets to relax! (6)

indicators: Just a couple of drops of

indicatorNotes.Just a couple of drops of: only two drops are taken, so only the first two letters

blocks.clueFragment: Just a couple of drops of semen
blocks.note: the first two letters of semen
a date is someone you are going out with

annotation.surface: A saucy line about a boyfriend unwinding after sex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relax' is transitive here: to sedate someone is to relax them.
annotation.definitionFit: To sedate someone is to relax them, usually with a drug.

entries.clue: Large expanse ripe for development — look into it (7)

indicatorNotes.for development: something ripe for development is due to be reshaped, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.into: the look goes inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: RIPE rearranged
an air is a look or manner

annotation.surface: An estate agent's pitch for a big plot of land waiting to be built on: take a look.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look into it' reads as an invitation to investigate; 'it' points back to the rearranged letters, and the look splits them after the second letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: North America's grassland plains stretch for hundreds of miles.

entries.clue: Emission – tax to the limit (7)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Emission' is a noun and 'tax to the limit' a verb phrase; EXHAUST serves as both.

blocks.note: the fumes a car's engine gives out
a verb: to drain or use up completely

annotation.surface: A complaint about a pollution levy set as high as it can go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks like a levy on emissions but is a verb: to tax to the limit is to wear out.
annotation.definitionFit: Exhaust is both the fumes a vehicle emits and a verb meaning to drain completely.

entries.clue: Enterprising energy chief hoarding top grade (2-5)

indicatorNotes.hoarding: to hoard is to keep something inside, so GO and HEAD hold the A between them

blocks.note: go means energy or drive
a head is a chief
A is the top exam grade

annotation.surface: A business profile of a dynamic head of an energy company who keeps the best marks for himself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Energy chief' reads as the boss of a power company, but the two words are separate pieces that hold the grade between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an enterprising person pushes ahead with new ventures.

entries.clue: Vote for manual workers' demo? (4,2,5)

blocks.note: a vote taken by raising hands
hands are manual workers, and a demo is a show

annotation.surface: A union meeting deciding whether factory workers should go on a protest march.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'demo' looks like a street protest but is taken as a demonstration, a showing; 'hands' are labourers.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a vote counted by raised hands, and literally a display by hands, the old word for labourers.

entries.clue: (& 24ac.) Latest broadcast: politician's pretentious talk? (3)

blocks.note: hot news is the latest
to air a programme is to broadcast it

annotation.surface: A headline about the newest broadcast of a politician's empty speech.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two grid entries, the second at 24; 'broadcast' is a verb here, not the noun it seems.
annotation.definitionFit: Hot air is empty, boastful talk, the stock in trade of politicians.

entries.clue: A short time taken by Hunt, yet devastated an English region (9)

indicatorNotes.taken by: the short time is taken in by the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.devastated: devastation leaves things in ruins, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: HUNT YET rearranged
a mo is a moment

annotation.surface: News that a politician named Hunt had a brief spell in office and wrecked part of England.
annotation.walkthrough: Hunt is the surname of more than one Conservative minister, which makes it look like a name to keep. Tynemouth is a town and borough at the mouth of the River Tyne in north-east England.
annotation.definitionFit: Tynemouth is a coastal area of north-east England.

entries.clue: Disreputable, negative rubbish about acknowledgements of liability (9)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: no is a negative answer
rot means nonsense, rubbish
an IOU (I owe you) is a written acknowledgement of a debt

annotation.surface: A damning report on a shady firm's refusal to own up to its debts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', linking the rubbish to the IOUs, but it tells you to turn the rubbish round.
annotation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, disreputable.

entries.clue: Commonplace stink associated with bass? (7)

blocks.note: a hum is a bad smell
a bass drum is the big drum of a kit; 'perhaps' is signalled by the question mark

annotation.surface: A dull joke about the smell of a fish, the bass.
annotation.walkthrough: Bass reads as the fish, which fits 'stink', but it is the musical sense: a bass drum. 'Hum' for a smell is British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something humdrum is dull and ordinary, as commonplace things are.

entries.clue: Thus having an erection for a starter? (4)

blocks.note: so means thus
the obvious slang sense

annotation.surface: A smutty joke about a man aroused before things have properly begun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A starter' reads as a beginning, but it is the first course of a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: soup is one of the dishes served as a first course.

entries.clue: Last composed Don't Panic (4,4)

blocks.note: to last is to stay the course, endure
composed means calm

annotation.surface: A note that 'Don't Panic' was the final thing someone wrote.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last composed' suggests a final composition, or 'composed' as an anagram sign for LAST; both are false, since STAY and CALM are plain synonyms.
annotation.definitionFit: Stay calm is the direct instruction 'don't panic'.

entries.clue: Butt, bust operated on (4)

indicatorNotes.operated on: surgery rearranges things, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A cosmetic-surgery tally: bottom and chest both done.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butt' and 'bust' look like two body parts on a surgeon's list; butt is the definition, in its sense of a stub.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the smoker's sense: the leftover end of a cigarette.

entries.clue: Crass ex-PM, ball trapped, needs hospital (7)

indicatorNotes.trapped: the ball is trapped inside the ex-PM
indicatorNotes.needs: the hospital is added at the end

blocks.note: Boris Johnson, former UK prime minister
O is round, like a ball
H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital

annotation.surface: Tabloid gloating that a boorish former prime minister has hurt his groin and needs treatment.
annotation.walkthrough: The ball goes after the B: B(O)ORIS. Boris Johnson was UK prime minister from 2019 to 2022.
annotation.definitionFit: Boorish means crass and ill-mannered.

entries.clue: Bloated corporation at end of the trail (9)

blocks.note: a corporation is an old joke word for a pot belly
last letter of 'the'
a scent is the trail a hound follows

annotation.surface: A swipe at a fat company reaching the end of the line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a company, but it is dated British humour for a large belly, as is TUM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tumescent is the medical word for swollen.

entries.clue: Sneak dick between legs, perhaps (7)

indicatorNotes.between: the dick goes between the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.perhaps: 'legs, perhaps' is only one possible version of legs, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: LEGS rearranged
a dick is a fool, and so is a mug

annotation.surface: A crude image of someone hiding something between their thighs to get it past customs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dick' reads as anatomy, but it is the insult: a dick and a mug are both idiots. 'Perhaps' looks like hedging but marks the jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to sneak goods past a border is to get them through illicitly.

entries.clue: Scandalous affair material (6)

indicatorNotes.Scandalous: something scandalous is disgraceful, out of order, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A tabloid phrase: scandalous affair material.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' seems to mean gossip-worthy content, but it is the definition: a fabric-like substance.
annotation.definitionFit: Raffia is palm fibre used as a material for weaving and tying.

entries.clue: see 13ac. (3)
Chance of corrupted input, or typo? (11)

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A programmer wondering whether a bug came from bad data or a slip of the keyboard.
annotation.walkthrough: The computing words make 'corrupted' look literal, but it is only the jumble sign.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an opportunity is a favourable moment to act.

entries.clue: Prized example of peer under pressure (5)

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure

annotation.surface: A model case of a young person resisting peer pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peer under pressure' looks like 'peer pressure', but splits into an earl sitting beneath P.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative use: the word means the finest of its kind, as in 'a pearl among men'.

entries.clue: Archer happy to get this meal when ditching date? (5)

blocks.note: dinner is a meal

entries.clue: How an habitual drinker appears to gain one state (7)

entries.clue: Mobile meant to suppress a German tone (7)

blocks.note: MEANT rearranged
used as it stands
G is the standard abbreviation for German

annotation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red tone of colour.

entries.clue: Seat from where many a politician's speech originates? (8)

annotation.definition: Seat from where many a politician's speech originates?

blocks.note: the surface wants a seat in Parliament; the setter means the seat you sit on, the backside

blocks.clueFragment: from where many a politician's speech originates?
blocks.note: the jibe is that politicians talk out of their backsides, spouting nonsense

annotation.surface: A question about which parliamentary seat a politician's speeches come from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seat' looks like a constituency, but it is the bottom; 'talking out of your arse' is British slang for spouting nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: The arsehole is, literally, an opening in the seat, and figuratively where nonsense comes from.

entries.clue: Ultimately, Senator Vance acted weird for a celebrated winner (3,3)

indicatorNotes.Ultimately: take only the last letter of each word

blocks.note: last letters of Senator, Vance, acted
rum is British slang for odd

annotation.surface: A jab at JD Vance for behaving oddly in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Weird' looks like part of the run of final letters, but is RUM. Red Rum was a racehorse that won the Grand National, Britain's great steeplechase, three times.
annotation.definitionFit: Red Rum is the most celebrated winner in Grand National history.
